editorial.headline: Precious-Metal Jewellery Manufacturing, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the making of body-worn precious-metal jewellery, with national PMA openness set against a clear Bali registration block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 32112 is about the manufacture of jewellery whose main material is precious metal: gold, platinum, and silver. The record describes articles worn on the body, on human clothing, or on pet animals, including rings, necklaces, bracelets, earrings, brooches, belts, buttons, and their parts and accessories. In plain English, this is the industrial activity behind precious-metal jewellery as a made product, not merely the trading or display of finished pieces.

The scope is specific enough to matter. The core test is the main material and the function of the article: precious metal, made into jewellery or related accessories. The record also draws one boundary around the activity by excluding imitation jewellery, so the editorial centre of this code remains genuine precious-metal manufacture rather than lookalike ornamentation. That distinction keeps the category anchored in production, material, and finished wearable form.

On business scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so it is not framed only as a large factory category or only as an artisan-sized activity. A small workshop making silver earrings and a larger operation producing gold rings both sit inside the same recorded scale envelope, as long as the activity remains within the described manufacture of precious-metal jewellery and its parts or accessories.

The national-versus-Bali picture is the decisive point. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, with the source recorded as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. But Bali is not nationally neutral here. The Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO, and the record marks it as blocked: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule is broader and clearer still: Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest reading is simple: this activity is foreign-open nationally, but a foreigner cannot register it as PMA in Bali today under the Bali-side block recorded here.
